tagline: Six and a half miles, with the red rocks closing in.
intro: Past the turn for Page Springs, SR 89A runs as a wide divided highway over rolling ground toward Sedona. Ahead to the east the red rock country inches closer and grows more dominant with every mile. Behind to the west lie Cottonwood and Clarkdale, and Jerome clinging to the side of Mingus Mountain.
It is a short road, six and a half miles to the Sedona line. Along the way there is a turn for Red Rock State Park, where nearly a mile and a half of Oak Creek runs through a red sandstone canyon.

moments.title: Page Springs Fish Hatchery
moments.text: Beside Oak Creek since 1932, the hatchery draws a steady 68-degree spring water all year and turns out nearly 700,000 trout annually.

moments.title: Dry Creek
moments.text: The creek that gives the road its name lives up to it most of the year, until early spring sends down snowmelt from the back country between Flagstaff and Sedona.

moments.title: Sedona
moments.text: Named for Sedona Schnebly, whose mother claimed she made the name up because it sounded pretty. In more than sixty films the rocks were passed off as Texas, California or Nevada.
